strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Build a personal weak-network VPN for OpenWrt/Linux to Linux or Windows using unordered FakeTCP/FEC carriers plus a native standards-compliant DTLS 1.3 WBD security/session layer. Xray/VLESS/Vision/REALITY, WireGuard and Android are not part of the V2.1 product stack.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: V2-M2 native WBD DTLS 1.3 security shim; M2A handshake/identity gate passed, M2B datagram independence active
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Keep M2 on one DTLS association and one raw lane. Do not add custom FEC, two lanes, kernel-anchor work, native TUN/session features, Auto, custom post-handshake crypto or detector-specific fingerprint shaping. Prove datagram independence before raw/FEC integration.

continuation_cursor.current_task: V2-M2B: implement and locally qualify a bidirectional DTLS 1.3 UDP datagram shim using the M2A-qualified wolfSSL configuration. Prove one input UDP datagram maps to one DTLS application write/read and that loss of one encrypted application datagram does not prevent a later application datagram from being authenticated and delivered.
continuation_cursor.why_now: Certificate identity and the exact DTLS 1.3 implementation are now independently proven. The next structural risk is accidentally rebuilding ordered delivery above DTLS. A plain-UDP shim/drop test isolates that property before UDPspeeder or udp2raw are introduced.
continuation_cursor.done_when: A local client/server shim maintains one DTLS 1.3 association, relays multiple bidirectional UDP application datagrams without merging them into a reliable stream, and a deterministic proxy that drops one post-handshake DTLS application datagram demonstrates that a later record is still independently authenticated/decrypted/delivered. The valid certificate/hostname path remains required. Record/application byte counts and observed drop index are recorded. No FEC or FakeTCP is present in this M2B gate.
continuation_cursor.next_atomic_action: V2-M2B: add a minimal wolfSSL DTLS 1.3 UDP relay with client plaintext-listen and server plaintext-target modes. Run it first over direct localhost UDP with a generated wbd.test certificate. Then place a deterministic UDP proxy between the DTLS peers, allow the handshake to finish, drop exactly one DTLS application datagram, and send numbered application datagrams so delivery of a later number proves no record-order HOL. Commit only after both direct relay and drop-one-record tests pass.
